problems.claimed: Safe by the stated rule: the existing max-width is already in ch, and .methodBody is a full-width prose column — the only prose child of .method, which is a plain padded block, not a grid or flex container. 88ch was well past a comfortable measure.
problems.problem: .methodBody is NOT a full-width prose column — it is the sole child of .method (line 207), a VISIBLE bordered, gold-washed callout box that spans the whole 1100px wrap. Rule 4's safe case is a block that already fills its own width; here the box's 1px gold border and background are drawn at ~1036px inner width while the text collapses to var(--measure) = 62ch ≈ 560px at 16px Geist. That leaves ~475px of empty washed panel to the right of every single line, and the border no longer frames the text it exists to frame. Rule 6 forbids narrowing .method itself to compensate, so applying this change has no in-scope fix. Separately, the stated height arithmetic is wrong for the same reason as the .intro finding: '15.5*1.75 = 27.1 vs 16*1.6 = 25.6 per line, so the box's total height barely moves' compares per-line height only and ignores that 88ch -> 62ch cuts ~30% of the characters per line. The paragraph is ~560 characters: ~6.5 lines at 88ch/15.5px (≈176px) becomes ~9 lines at 62ch/16px (≈230px). The box grows ~55px, it does not 'barely move', and the 28px 32px padding is being justified against a number that never happens.
problems.correction: FLAG this one instead of changing it, per rule 4's escape hatch. Take the size and line-height (15.5px -> var(--type-body), 1.75 -> var(--type-body-lh)) and leave max-width: 88ch alone, with a note that the callout needs a container decision — either .method itself narrows or the measure does — which is out of scope for a type-scale pass. If it is applied anyway, the honest 'why' is: the box grows ~55px taller and ~475px of it goes empty.

problems.claimed: Already 18px, so this is a pure token swap today — but it also buys the automatic 20px bump at >=900px that the token carries. / Slight tightening (18px: 28.8px -> 27px per line); the 20px 0 0 margin above still reads correctly, no margin change needed.
problems.problem: The 18px branch of --type-lede is UNREACHABLE on this surface, so neither claim describes anything that happens. .intro lives inside .desktopOnly, which is display:none under @media (max-width: 900px) (line 6); globals.css:398 sets --type-lede: 20px under @media (min-width: 900px). The two ranges are complementary — at every viewport where .intro is painted, the token resolves to 20px. So this is not a 'pure token swap today', it is an 18px -> 20px size increase, and the leading goes 18*1.6 = 28.8px -> 20*1.5 = 30px per line, i.e. each line gets TALLER, not the '27px' tightening claimed. Compounded with change 3 (74ch -> 62ch), the hero lede drops from ~74 to ~62 characters per line at a larger size: the ~460-character paragraph goes from ~6 lines to ~8, and the block grows from ~173px to ~240px. That pushes .reviewed, the whole contents grid and every finding down ~65px. The change is still the right one; the justification is backwards, and the 'no margin change needed' conclusion is drawn from the wrong direction of movement.
problems.correction: Keep both changes but rewrite the why: '.intro renders only above 900px, where --type-lede is already 20px, so this is an 18 -> 20px bump, not a swap. With the measure narrowing to 62ch the hero lede gains ~2 lines and ~65px of height; margin: 20px 0 0 still reads correctly, but everything below the hero shifts down.' Same rewrite is needed on change 3, which calls the narrowing '~74 to 62 characters' without noting it costs lines.

problems.claimed: OPEN QUESTION: ...the paragraphs would stop filling the track they were sized to fill and the column would end short of the chart's border-left rule.
problems.problem: The premise is wrong, so the question is posed against a constraint that does not exist. .findingBody (line 147) carries align-items: start, which means .chartCol is start-aligned and sized to ITS OWN content — its border-left (line 170) is already only as tall as the chart, never as tall as the grid row. Prose length has no relationship to that rule today, so 'the column would end short of the chart's border-left' cannot happen whether or not the measure is applied. (For the same reason, change 13's line-height 1.7 -> 1.6 shortening the prose by ~6% also cannot shorten or orphan that border — worth stating, since it is the one thing a reviewer would worry about there.) The genuine consideration is narrower: at the 1180px wrap the 1.35fr track is ~607px and 62ch at 16px is ~560px, so the measure would take effect and leave ~47px of unused track — a visible ragged right edge against a column whose sibling starts at a fixed offset.
problems.correction: Re-pose the question against the real trade-off: 'The grid is align-items:start, so the chart's border-left is content-height and prose length does not interact with it. Applying the measure narrows the prose ~47px inside its 607px track (visible slack at the 1180px wrap) and does real work below 1240px where the grid collapses to 1fr. Apply, or let the track be the measure?' Keep the decision to NOT apply it — that part is right.

problems.claimed: line 138 = .statL font-size 11px -> var(--type-label); line 139 = .statL letter-spacing 0.11em -> var(--type-label-tracking). Same for .chartLabel at lines 173/174.
problems.problem: Both pairs are off by one, in the same direction, for the same reason: .statL and .chartLabel are the only two label rules in the file that declare font-weight: 700 between font-family and font-size, and the plan counted past it. Line 138 is 'font-weight: 700;' and 139 is 'font-size: 11px;' (140 is letter-spacing); line 173 is 'font-weight: 700;' and 174 is 'font-size: 11px;' (175 is letter-spacing). The plan's OWN open question cites .statL line 144 for line-height: 1.4, which is correct — so the file is inconsistent with itself about where .statL's declarations are. If these are applied by line number rather than by selector+property, the first edit in each pair rewrites 'font-weight: 700' into 'font-size: var(--type-label)', silently stripping the 700 weight from two Space Mono labels and leaving a duplicate font-size on the next line. Every other line number in the plan checks out (17, 18, 32, 39, 40, 93, 94, 149, 181, 197-200, 217).
problems.correction: font-size for .statL is line 139 and letter-spacing 140; font-size for .chartLabel is 174 and letter-spacing 175. Fix all four before any mechanical application.

problems.claimed: Pinning 1.5 makes the step complete and self-contained. .barHead is align-items:baseline, so the baseline the value aligns to does not move.
problems.problem: Baseline alignment is exactly what makes this claim false. In a baseline-aligned flex line the item with the largest above-baseline extent sets where the shared baseline sits relative to the line-box top, and half-leading is part of that extent. .barName (13.5px) is larger than .barValue (12px), so .barName IS the item setting the baseline. It currently inherits line-height 1.6 from body (globals.css:463) = 21.6px; pinning 1.5 gives 20.25px, removing ~0.7px of half-leading above the baseline. The baseline therefore moves up relative to the row top, .barHead's height drops ~1.35px, and with ~5 bars plus 13px gaps the chart column shortens ~7px per finding. Nothing breaks — but the stated reason for it being safe is the opposite of the mechanism, and 'the value does not move' is precisely what a baseline row cannot promise when you change the taller item's leading.
problems.correction: Keep the change, fix the why: '.barName inherits 1.6 from body (21.6px); 1.5 gives 20.25px. It is the taller item in a baseline-aligned flex row, so it sets the baseline — each .barHead loses ~1.35px and the chart column shortens ~7px. .barValue keeps its position relative to the name; only the row box tightens.'

problems.claimed: (no entry — .findingLink is absent from all 24 changes and from the open questions)

It is font-family mono, font-weight 700, font-size 11px, text-transform uppercase — the same shape as .kicker, .reviewed, .findingKicker, .statL and .chartLabel, all five of which get the token — but its letter-spacing is 0.12em, the only value on the page that DIFFERS from --type-label-tracking (0.11em). So it is also the only one where tokenising would actually change a computed value. Under this lens leaving it alone is the correct call — it sits in a pill with min-height: 44px and padding: 0 18px, a tap target whose width is set by content, and 0.12em -> 0.11em would narrow every pill by ~1px per 10 characters and could reflow the flex-wrap in .findingLinks — but the plan never says that, so a reviewer cannot tell whether it was a decision or an oversight.
problems.correction: Add a change:false entry for .findingLink lines 162-163 stating the reason: 'label-role, but the only tracking on the page that is not 0.11em, and it sits inside a 44px min-height tap target in a flex-wrap row — tokenising it would narrow every pill and could change where .findingLinks wraps. Left at 0.12em deliberately.' Same treatment would be worth giving .barValue (lines 184-191, 12px mono, kept mono for font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums).

problems.claimed: line 173, .chartLabel, property font-size, from 11px → var(--type-label)

problems.correction: Retarget: font-size at line 174, letter-spacing at line 175. (.kicker 17/18, .reviewed 39/40, .findingKicker 93/94 and .chartNote 197-200 were all checked and ARE correct — only .statL and .chartLabel drifted, both by exactly one line.)

problems.claimed: "Already 18px, so this is a pure token swap today" / line-height "Slight tightening (18px: 28.8px -> 27px per line)"

So at every viewport where .intro is actually painted, the token is 20px, never 18px. problems.claimed: Open question: "is [mobileAnalysis.module.css] queued as its own surface? If it is not, every change above lands for desktop readers only."

On a phone it is a running prose block at BELOW caption size wearing the secondary-label colour — a double failure of rules 3 and 5 in one declaration, and the single worst-reading text on the page.

problems.claimed: (not covered by the plan)

problems.claimed: "Brings the one off-value tracking on the page (0.1em) onto the label token"
problems.problem: False. The page carries three off-token trackings on mono label-family rules, not one: .reviewed 0.1em (line 40), .findingLink 0.12em (line 163), .chartNote 0.08em (line 199). Decide explicitly and record it (change:false with the rule-1 reason, or tokenise 0.12em → var(--type-label-tracking)); do not leave it unmentioned.

problems.problem: The rule declares no font-weight — lines 33-43 set font-family, font-size, letter-spacing, text-transform and colour only, so .reviewed renders at the inherited 400. problems.claimed: Open question quotes .statL wrapping as "Chart entries in the UK"; the change's why quotes "Chart entries", "No. 1s" and calls them "a table-header-style label, not a sentence"
problems.problem: No such label exists. app/lib/analysisFindings.ts:75-77, 102-104, 132-134, 162-164 give the real set: "Dai Dai country No. 1s", "UK chart entries", "of them, from one song", "releases that ever hit No. 1", "country awarded them". "of them, from one song" is a dependent clause that only reads as a continuation of the 52px number above it, not a table header — the "not a sentence" basis for the label step is weaker than stated, and the wrap question was asked about a string that isn't in the data.

problems.claimed: "Safe by the stated rule... 88ch was well past a comfortable measure"
problems.problem: Safe by rule 4 (ch → ch, plain block parent) — .method at line 207 is a padded bordered div, confirmed not a grid or flex container, so the mechanical judgement holds. But the consequence is not noted: .method's inner width is ~1036px at the 1180px wrap, and 62ch at 16px Geist is ~510px. The gold-tinted, gold-bordered callout keeps its full width while its only content shrinks to under half of it, leaving ~500px of empty tinted panel to the right of every line. That is a composition change to a boxed element, not just a measure change to prose.

problems.claimed: Open question: "is one lede-sized opening paragraph per section intended?"
problems.problem: Real, and the question understates it. The correction paragraph is not an opening paragraph — it is the section's ONLY paragraph (the section is h2 + p + a button link, lines 197-208). problems.problem: .q on mobileFaqSection is not a bare heading — FaqList renders a <button class=.toggle> inside it (FaqList.tsx:95-108), and .toggle is `display:flex; align-items:flex-start` with .glyph as a fixed sibling: `width:16px; font-size:15px; line-height:inherit`. problems.problem: The rationale describes a rendering case that cannot occur on this surface. .body keeps margin: 13px 0 0 while its leading goes from 21.6px (13.5 x 1.6) to 25.6px (16 x 1.6). The gap BETWEEN paragraphs becomes half the space INSIDE one, so paragraph boundaries stop reading. This is not hypothetical on this screen: MobileAnalysis.tsx lines 82-86 map f.body into sibling

elements, and all four findings carry exactly three paragraphs (app/lib/analysisFindings.ts lines 79-83, 106-112, 136-142, 166-170), so eight boundaries collapse. problems.problem: The plan tokenises .findingKicker and .kicker font-size and letter-spacing but adds no line-height, while justifying the NEW line-height on .reviewed (change 15) with "size and leading are always used as a pair". Neither label rule declares one today, and --type-label-lh (1.2) exists. Otherwise the next pass 'completes' the tokenisation and breaks it.

problems.problem: The plan emits zero change:false entries, so the count does not add up against rule 7. Two rules it touches are already correct on a dimension it never records — .lede (line 96) and .body (line 168) both already carry color: var(--text-body), the reading colour, which is exactly the correction the plan makes a point of on .checkBody. And .statLabel (11px Space Mono, letter-spacing 0.05em, var(--text-muted)) is a label-role rule the plan neither tokenises nor accounts for, while it does tokenise the two other label rules on the same screen — leaving one 11px mono label at 0.05em tracking next to two at 0.11em.
problems.claimed: 18 changes, no change:false entries.

Note that tokenising it WOULD move tracking 0.05em -> 0.11em and widen the labels inside grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0,1fr)) cells at 320px, so change:false is likely the right call.

problems.problem: The stated mechanism for the new .reviewed line-height is wrong, even though the conclusion holds. align-items: center does not absorb a line-height change: it centres items within a flex line whose cross size the tallest item SETS, and the text is that item, so its line box is the row height. The row goes from 11 x 1.6 (body's line-height, globals.css line 463) = 17.6px to 12.5 x 1.45 = 18.1px — a real +0.5px, imperceptible by arithmetic, not by absorption. The risk is that this justification, reused on a row where the delta is larger, licenses a change that does move the layout.

problems.correction: Restate as: the row is sized by the text item's line box, which goes 17.6px -> 18.1px against body's inherited 1.6 (globals.css line 463); +0.5px, and .reviewedDot is flex:none at 7px so it does not set the cross size.

problems.claimed: "At the 1240px cap the answer track is ~731px, which at 16px Geist is ~91ch" and "the 1.6fr column gains ~170px of trailing space on a laptop".
problems.problem: There is no 1240px cap on this page. `.wrap` (line 6, max-width: 1240px) is declared in song.module.css but never applied: `grep styles.wrap` returns nothing in app/music/[song]/page.tsx or app/music/albums/[album]/page.tsx. So the grid spans the viewport minus 80px, unbounded. On a 1728px laptop the 1.6fr answer track is ~1050px (~131ch), not 731px/91ch; on a 2560px monitor it is ~1610px. The measure problem is materially worse than the plan's own worst case, and the "~170px of trailing space" figure that the recommendation hesitates over is off by roughly 3x.

problems.claimed: "Risky because it grows every question row ~4-5px and the mobile gap under it is only 6px."
problems.problem: ~4-5px is the single-line delta (1.35x16 = 21.6px to 1.3x20 = 26px) and only holds if the question does not rewrap. On the phone accordion it does. At 375px the question's line box is 375 - 36 (gutter, .sectionPad line 333) - 16 (.glyph width) - 14 (.toggle gap) = ~309px; average Geist advance goes from ~8px at 16px to ~10.2px at 20px/600, so lines-per-question drops from ~38 chars to ~30. problems.claimed: Change 3's rationale: "faqList.module.css .glyph is `line-height: inherit` by design so the +/- glyph stays pinned to the question's first line — it follows this value rather than needing its own edit."
problems.problem: `line-height: inherit` passes the unitless *ratio* (1.3), not the question's line box. `.glyph` sets its own `font-size: 15px` (line 62), so its line box becomes 15 x 1.3 = 19.5px while the question's becomes 20 x 1.3 = 26px, and `.toggle` is `align-items: flex-start` (line 27) so both boxes start at the same top edge. Baseline offsets from that top: question ~16px ((26 - 24)/2 + 15), glyph ~12px ((19.5 - 18)/2 + 11.25) — a ~4px lift. Today the two boxes are 21.6px and 20.25px, a sub-1px difference, which is why the current pinning looks correct. The change quietly breaks the one behaviour its own rationale cites as evidence that no edit is needed, on the phone accordion only.
problems.correction: Either give `.glyph` the question's computed line box instead of the ratio — `line-height: calc(var(--type-h-prose) * var(--type-h-prose-lh))` in place of `inherit` — or raise it as a fourth open question alongside the 6px gap. Do not land change 3 with a rationale that asserts the glyph needs no edit.

Line 37: "a question is one ~21px line and growing every row to 44px would re-space two lists" — the song-page question becomes a ~26px line, and that sentence is the justification for the `inset: -11px 0` hit area on line 47 (the target grows to ~48px, which is fine, but the arithmetic no longer reads).

Note in the write-up that the 44px touch minimum still holds after the change (26 + 22 = 48px) and that the 36px inter-target clearance from `.faqItem { padding: 18px 0 }` (line 371) is unaffected.

problems.claimed: faqList.module.css .glyph is `line-height: inherit` by design so the +/- glyph stays pinned to the question's first line — it follows this value rather than needing its own edit.
problems.problem: A unitless line-height inherits the NUMBER, not the parent's used pixel height. `.toggle` takes `font: inherit` so it computes line-height 1.3; `.glyph` then computes 1.3 x its OWN 15px = 19.5px, not the question span's 1.3 x 20px = 26px. `.toggle` is `align-items: flex-start`, so the two line boxes are top-aligned and the glyph, centred in a 19.5px box, sits (26-19.5)/2 = 3.3px above the centre of the question's first line. Today the same arithmetic gives (21.6-20.25)/2 = 0.7px, which is why nobody has noticed. The change quadruples an error the plan believes it is immune to, on every phone FAQ row of 14 song pages and 8 album pages. Desktop is unaffected — `.toggle` is never rendered above 900px — so this is a mobile-only regression caused by a desktop-framed edit.
problems.correction: Keep change #3, but pin the glyph in the same commit: on `.glyph`, replace `line-height: inherit` with `line-height: calc(var(--type-h-prose) * var(--type-h-prose-lh))` so it takes the question's USED line box (26px) rather than re-deriving 1.3 from its own font-size. Delete the 'it follows this value' sentence from change #3's rationale — it is the reason the glyph was skipped and it is not true.

problems.problem: `.glyph { font-size: 15px }` is a hard-coded size tuned against the 16px question it sits beside (94% of it). The question moves to 20px on the phone — the plan says so itself, via `font: inherit` on `.toggle` — and the glyph does not move, landing at 75%. This is the only piece of the phone accordion with its own size, and it is a mobile-only rule that exists to be read as part of the question row: one half of that row got a step of the scale and the other half was left at a number nobody re-derived.
problems.correction: Decide it explicitly rather than by omission. The `+/−` is a mono affordance, not prose, so it is out of the scale's four steps — but it should be re-tuned to the new question (17-18px keeps the 90%-ish relationship the row was drawn with), or the plan should state that 15px against 20px is the intended new proportion.
